summary: Cured Villager trades are not refreshing
description:
Steps to reproduce:

PART I:

First I spawned in a Villager, made hima cozy little ... house, and put a lectern in front of him, which resulted in the following Brain data:

{memories: {"minecraft:last_worked_at_poi": {value: 2305L}, "minecraft:job_site": {value: {pos: [I; -232, 128, 110], dimension: "minecraft:overworld"}}}}

then I traded with him and waited around a bit for him to do his work routine which resulted in the following:

{memories: {"minecraft:last_worked_at_poi": {value: 19582L}, "minecraft:job_site": {value: {pos: [I; -232, 128, 110], dimension: "minecraft:overworld"}}}

then a zombie "snuck" in to my little "house" (totally on accident), and I converted the poor fella into a villager again after he was inevitably munched on by the zombie.

and I do understand that that must have messed with his Brain quite a bit, but he lost all information in there resulting in the following

{memories: {}}

so he lost his job_site and all other valuable information, but I decided to just give him a new lectern (so he had two for the moment), which he cheerfully accepted by emitting green particles, a check on the data of him did reveal that there was nothing in Brain still (no change to above)

I then tried breaking and placing the workstation a couple times, which was acknowledged by green particles every time, but still his Brain showed signs of his previous affliction, and would not register the job_site again.

I also waited for a couple ingame days, sleeping through some nights, not sleeping through others without any luck of him realizing he's standing right infront of a suitable workstation.

I then tried placing other workstations, namely a composter and a grindstone, which was greeted by the same green particles emitted before.

This behaviour is not only frustrating but also it doesn't make much sense to me, that the villager would act this way.

PART II:

I then proceeded to add all other possible workstations, which were ALL acknowledged by our Librarian friend.

Guessing they would all be locked to the Librarian now I added two more villagers, without profession so he wouldn't be too lonely, and as I expected they weren't able to pick any of the 14 job sites available to them now (2 lecterns and 1 of each other type)

only after breaking and replacing the composter for example was one of the professionless villagers able to pick it up as his own.

Possibly useful information:

The workstations in Part 1 were always adjecent to the villager on foot level, so there should be no issue with pathfinding.

The Villager always stood on the same block for the entire process of Part 1.
Steps to Reproduce:
1. Spawn a villager and keep it at a fixed position.
2. Place a lectern directly adjacent to the villager at foot level.
3. Trade with the villager.
4. Wait at least a few minutes for the villager to perform its work routine.
5. Allow a zombie to attack the villager until it becomes a zombie villager.
6. Cure the zombie villager.
7. Wait until the conversion back into a villager is complete.
8. Place a new lectern directly adjacent to the cured villager, leaving the original lectern in place.
9. Wait until a couple of in-game days have passed, sleeping through some nights and not sleeping through others.
10. Observe that the cured villager emits green particles when given workstations but does not register a job site or refresh its trades.
Environment: Minecraft Java Edition Versions: 1.19 Release Candidate 2, 1.19
Observed Behavior:
### Actual behavior

After being cured, the villager’s `Brain.memories` tag becomes empty, including the `minecraft:job_site` and `minecraft:last_worked_at_poi` memories.

The villager retains its librarian profession and existing trades, but it does not appear to register or use a workstation afterward:

- Placing a lectern directly adjacent to the villager produces green particles, but does not add a `minecraft:job_site` memory.
- Breaking and replacing the lectern repeatedly has the same result.
- Waiting through multiple in-game days, including days with and without sleeping, does not restore the workstation memories or cause the villager to restock its trades.
- Placing other workstations, such as a composter or grindstone, also produces green particles, despite the villager not recording a corresponding job site.
- When additional unemployed villagers are nearby, the cured villager appears to claim or reserve the available workstations: the other villagers cannot claim them. Breaking and replacing a workstation is required before one of the unemployed villagers can claim it.

Thus, the cured villager emits the workstation-claim particles and seems to interfere with other villagers’ access to job sites, but does not regain a valid `job_site` memory or resume working and refreshing its trades.
Expected Behavior: After being cured, the villager should retain its profession and existing trade data, correctly recognize an adjacent suitable workstation, and reclaim its job site. It should be able to work there and refresh exhausted trades normally. Workstations not claimed by that villager should remain available for other unemployed villagers to recognize and claim, without requiring repeated breaking and replacing.
